title: Affine overlaps of affine charts of a separated space over an affine base
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $V$ an affine $S$-scheme, and $f:X\to V$ a separated morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space, lem-trf-space-qc-separated-etale-local]. Thus the representable diagonal $\Delta_f:X\to X\times_VX$ is a closed immersion on every scheme test [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let $u_i:U_i\to X$ for $i=0,1$ be etale maps from affine schemes, not necessarily surjective. Put $a_i=f\circ u_i:U_i\to V$ and $R=U_0\times_XU_1$ [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], with projections $r_i:R\to U_i$. Then $R$ is a scheme, the $r_i$ are etale, and its canonical map $j:R\to U_0\times_VU_1$ is a closed immersion of schemes. More precisely, there is a canonical isomorphism $R\simeq X\times_{X\times_VX}(U_0\times_VU_1)$ over $U_0\times_VU_1$, identifying $j$ with the scheme test of $\Delta_f$. The scheme $R$ is affine, and $a_0,a_1$ and $b=a_0\circ r_0=a_1\circ r_1:R\to V$ are quasi-compact separated morphisms of schemes, with their usual closed-diagonal and affine-test meanings. The fibre product of schemes is [def-pc-fibre-product]. No quasi-compactness hypothesis on $X$ or $f$ is required.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-presheaf-pullback-etale-point-lifting] to the singleton map $u_1$ and $G=h_{U_0}$: its representable-etale conclusion, which requires no joint surjectivity, makes $R$ a scheme and $r_0$ etale. Interchange $0,1$ for $r_1$. The algebraic-space and sheaf fibre products agree by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers].

source.place: Tag 041F (lemma-etale), (3), scheme-test base change; spaces.tex Tag 02X2 (lemma-fibre-product-spaces).

proof.text: Put $P=U_0\times_VU_1$. On any $S$-scheme $T$, a section of $X\times_{X\times_VX}P$ is a triple $(x,p_0,p_1)$ with $u_0(p_0)=x=u_1(p_1)$. Send it to $(p_0,p_1)\in R(T)$; the inverse adjoins $x=u_0(p_0)$. These maps commute with restrictions and preserve the projection to $P$. Thus they are inverse sheaf maps, hence the asserted canonical isomorphism. The fibre-product universal properties are [def-pc-fibre-product, lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers].

source.place: Tag 03M9 (lemma-pushforward), affine-target paragraph: R maps to U times_Y U; explicit mixed-chart diagonal test.

proof.text: The map $P\to X\times_VX$ has components $u_0\circ\mathrm{pr}_0,u_1\circ\mathrm{pr}_1$. By the definition of separatedness in [lem-trf-space-qc-separated-etale-local], its test of $\Delta_f$ is a closed immersion of schemes. Step 2 identifies this test with $j:R\to P$, including its map to $P$.

source.place: Tag 03HL (definition-separated), and Tag 03KM (lemma-separated-local); Tag 03M9 diagonal-test argument with separatedness.

proof.text: Choose spectra for the three affine schemes $U_0,U_1,V$; [def-weil-affine-spectrum] writes their maps as ring homomorphisms. Then [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] identifies $P$ with the spectrum of the tensor product of the two chart rings over the base ring. Since $P$ is affine, the affine description in [def-weil-closed-immersion] applied to $j$ over the whole of $P$ writes $R$ as the spectrum of a quotient ring. Hence $R$ is affine.

source.place: Tag 01JQ (lemma-fibre-product-affines), using Tag 01I4 (lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes); morphisms.tex Tag 01QO (lemma-closed-immersion), affine description.

proof.text: The singleton affine cover $\{V\}$ has affine inverse images $U_0,U_1,R$ under $a_0,a_1,b$. Thus [pqf-lem-affine-local-target] makes all three morphisms affine. Clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence] makes them quasi-compact and separated. The equality $a_0r_0=a_1r_1$ is the defining compatibility of $R$, and no step used quasi-compactness of $X$ or $f$.
